claim: Château de Meursault offers a Grands Terroirs guided cellar tour with 7-wine tasting at €59 (1h15-1h30, max 12 people); Prestige private tour with 8 wines at €105; Exclusive vineyard+cellar at €175; walk-in tastings from €35 daily 10-11:30 and 14-17 subject to availability.
quote: GRANDS TERROIRS €59 — Guided visit of the cellars followed by a tasting of 7 wines. PRESTIGE €105 — Private cellar tour, tasting of 8 prestigious wines. EXCLUSIVE €175. Walk-in tastings from €35.

claim: In Santenay, Château Philippe le Hardi accepts visits from €11/adult, Château de la Crée from €22/adult and Domaine Evenstad from €19/adult, all with free booking and instant confirmation; advance reservation advised.
quote: Château Philippe le Hardi From €11/adult … Château de la Crée From €22/adult … Domaine Evenstad From €19/adult … whether you are visiting a famous winery or a family-owned winery, we advise you to book in advance.

claim: In Puligny-Montrachet, Maison Chanzy offers a tasting cellar/wine bar visit from €28/adult; nearby in Pommard Maison Jean-Marc Boillot has tastings from €12/adult, with free online booking up to 30 minutes prior.
quote: Maison Chanzy à Puligny-Montrachet From €28 / adult … Maison Jean-Marc Boillot From €12 / adult … Bookable Up to 30 minutes prior.

claim: Château de Saint-Aubin / Maison Prosper Maufoux runs the 'Expérience Prosper' at €37 pp (5 wines incl. 2 Premiers Crus, 1h) and 'Expérience Prestige' at €62 pp (6 wines incl. 4 Premiers Crus with Burgundy snacks, 1h30), by reservation only.
quote: Expérience Prosper: €37 per person … 5 wines tasted (2 Premiers Crus) … lasting 1 hour, by reservation only. Expérience Prestige: €62 per person … 6 wines tasted including 4 Premiers Crus, accompanied by Burgundy snacks, lasting 1 hour 30 minutes, by reservation only.

claim: Château de Pommard tasting experiences range €30-€260 and are offered daily (reduced winter hours); reservations are required but free up to 4 hours before, free cancellation up to 2 hours before, with WSET-trained advisors guiding 6-wine tastings in the Clos Marey-Monge cellars.
quote: The price of Château de Pommard experiences varies between €30.00 and €260.00 … you can book for free up to 4 hours before … cancel your booking free of charge up to 2 hours before … taste six wines from Château de Pommard and Famille Carabello-Baum.

claim: Caves Patriarche in Beaune (largest cellar in Burgundy, 5 km of 13th-century galleries, 2M bottles) runs a daily self-guided audio tour with sommelier-poured tasting of 6 wines (3 whites/3 reds incl. Meursault and Nuits-St-Georges 1er Cru) from 2 Jan to 30 Dec 2026, 9:30-11:00 and 14:00-17:00.
quote: available daily from 2 January to 30 December 2026 … self-guided tour … four video points in nine languages … tasting of six Grands Vins de Bourgogne wines with our sommeliers … three whites (Savigny les Beaune, Rully, Meursault) and three reds (Santenay, Beaune 1er Cru, Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru).

claim: Beaune Tourism's 10 must-see wineries within day-trip range of Chagny include Caves Patriarche, Maison Champy (1720, Eiffel-designed winery), Bouchard Père et Fils (Château de Beaune, by reservation only), Château de Pommard, Château Meursault, Château Philippe le Hardi in Santenay, Château de Saint-Aubin, and Henri de Villamont in Savigny-lès-Beaune.
quote: Caves Patriarche – Beaune … Maison Champy – Beaune … Maison Bouchard Père et Fils – Beaune … Château de Pommard … Château Meursault … Château Philippe le Hardi – Santenay … Château de Saint-Aubin … Henri de Villamont – Savigny-les-Beaune.

claim: Most Burgundy domaines close for lunch (noon-14:00) and all day Sunday; Patriarche and Bouchard Aîné are notable Beaune cellars that stay open on Sundays, and many small producers expect prior appointment by email or phone.
quote: many shops and domains are closed everyday between noon and 2pm and all day on Sundays. However, there are some exceptions. Cellars in Beaune that are open on Sundays include Patriarche (the biggest cellars in Burgundy) and Bouchard Aîné & Fils cellars.

claim: In Aloxe-Corton, Domaine Comte Senard (Grands Crus producer since 1857) and Maison Champy are the most-booked tasting visits, with instant confirmation and free cancellation; Château Corton C (7 ha, run by Caroline Frey) is also in the village.
quote: The most popular wineries in the Aloxe Corton appellation are: Caveau Moillard - Meursault, Domaine Comte Senard, and Maison Champy … Domaine Comte Senard, known for its Grands Crus, has been operating since 1857 in the small village of Aloxe-Corton.

claim: Domaine Bader-Mimeur in Chassagne-Montrachet (family estate since 1919) is open daily 9:30-18:00 and uniquely accepts walk-in tour and tasting visits, though appointment is preferred.
quote: Domaine Bader-Mimeur is a family estate settled in Chassagne-Montrachet since 1919. They are open everyday from 9:30 am to 6:00 pm, with appointment would be better … visitors can pop in when passing and receive a tour and tasting.

claim: Hôtel-Dieu opens 9am–7:30pm continuously April 1–Nov 15 2026; off-season 9am–12:30pm and 2–6:30pm; open every day of the year, last ticket 1h before closing.
quote: January 1 – March 31: 9 AM–12:30 PM & 2–6:30 PM ... April 1 – November 15: 9 AM–7:30 PM ... November 16 – December 31: 9 AM–12:30 PM & 2–6:30 PM

claim: Base Hôtel-Dieu ticket is €9.50, reduced €6.25 (youth 6–17, students, jobseekers); free under 6.
quote: The basic Hôtel-Dieu ticket is €9.50, with a reduced price of €6.25 for students, large families, CEZAM card holders, tour guides, job seekers, and RSA beneficiaries.

claim: Marché aux Vins self-guided Découverte (5 wines) costs €25 online/€29 on-site; Prestige (7 wines) €49/€59; guided Exclusive €65; Tailor-made from €99.
quote: Découverte (5 wines): €25 online / €29 on-site ... Prestige (7 wines): €49 online / €59 on-site ... Exclusive (7 wines): €65 (max 10 people) ... Tailor-made (8 wines): From €99

claim: The Cité des Climats et Vins de Bourgogne in Beaune is a landmark building with 24-metre-high vine-like tendrils at 21 avenue Charles de Gaulle, devoted to the UNESCO-listed Climats of Burgundy.
quote: bright tendrils rising 24 meters high, evoking the way vines coil around trellises ... 21 avenue Charles de Gaulle, 21200 Beaune

claim: Cité tour costs €14.50 with reduced rates; open daily 10am–6pm low/mid season, 10am–7pm June 1–Sept 30 2026; annual closure Jan 5–18, 2026; reservation required.
quote: From June 1 to September 30, 2026 (high season): open every day from 10am to 7pm ... The price of experiences is €14.50 ... annual closure from January 5 to 18, 2026.

claim: Patriarche Père & Fils runs self-guided cellar visits with sommelier-led tasting of 6 Burgundy wines daily Jan 2–Dec 30 2026, departures 9:45am–4:45pm, capped at 10 per slot.
quote: departures at 9:45 am, 10:15 am, 10:45 am, 2:15 pm, 2:45 pm, 3:15 pm, 3:45 pm, 4:15 pm, and 4:45 pm, limited to 10 people per departure

claim: Patriarche occupies the former Visitandines convent and holds Burgundy's largest cellars (about 5 km of galleries).
quote: Maison Patriarche Père et Fils offers a self-guided tour of Burgundy's largest wine cellars

claim: Maison Joseph Drouhin's Oenothèque at 1 Cour du Parlement de Bourgogne offers visits by appointment only at 10am, 2pm and 4pm Monday–Saturday; tastings €38, €70 or €120 per person.
quote: visits at 10:00 am, 2:00 pm and 4 pm every day from Monday to Saturday included ... Tasting prices are 38€, 70€, or 120€ per person.

claim: Drouhin's cellars cover roughly 1 hectare in Beaune's historic centre between the Hospice and Notre-Dame, with sections dating to the Dukes of Burgundy and the Kings of France.
quote: These historical cellars cover approximately 1 hectare in the historical centre of Beaune, between the Hospice de Beaune and Notre-Dame Church

claim: Bouchard Aîné & Fils' '5 Senses' guided tour in 18th-century cellars tastes 5 wines (2 white, 3 red, Village and Premier Cru); departures 10:30, 11:30, 14:30, 16:00, 17:00, max 20 per group.
quote: Guided tours depart at 10:30, 11:30, 14:30, 16:00 and 17:00 with a limited number of places per tour (20) ... tasting of 5 wines including 2 white, 3 red, Village and Premier Crus

claim: Bouchard Père et Fils, founded 1731, owns 130 hectares in the Côte d'Or including 74 ha of premiers crus and 12 ha of grands crus; tours of the 15th-century Château de Beaune cellars include tastings of 6 or 8 wines.
quote: founded in 1731 by Michel Bouchard ... 130 hectares, including 74 hectares of premier crus and 12 hectares of grand crus vines ... private tours of the cellars of Château de Beaune, which is a 15th century fortress

claim: Moutarderie Fallot's Parcours Découvertes (Discovery Trail) runs daily Jan 2–Dec 31 2026 at 10am, 11:30am, 3pm, 4:30pm; €12 adult, €9 child/concession; shop open until 6pm.
quote: Every day from 2 January to 31 December 2026: 10am, 11.30am (tour in French AND English), 3pm, 4.30pm ... Adult rate: €12 (18 years and over) ... Child rate: €9

claim: Beaune's main weekly food market runs every Saturday 7am–1pm across Place de la Halle, Place Fleury and Avenue de la République with around 180 stalls of produce, cheese, meat, spices and organic farms.
quote: The market operates every Saturday from 7 AM to 1 PM ... around 180 traders ... fruit and vegetables, meat, cheeses, spices, roasters, organic produce and products from small farms

quote: Le château de La Rochepot officiellement confisqué à son ancien propriétaire ukrainien... La cour d'appel de Metz a officiellement prononcé la confiscation du château.

claim: The local Nolay tourist office confirms Château de La Rochepot is closed to the public and can only be photographed from the outside.
quote: The château is closed to the public – it can only be to photographed from the outside.

claim: Château de Couches (the 'Marguerite de Bourgogne' fortress, ~15 km west of Chagny) runs guided visits with an €8 flat-rate audio guide and major 2026 events including Journées du Patrimoine (19-20 Sept), Halloween (21 Oct-1 Nov) and Noël au Château (19-30 Dec).
quote: Les journées du patrimoine... Halloween... Noël au Château... audio guide... 8€

claim: Château de Rully (≈5 km from Chagny) is a privately owned medieval château offering guided interior tours of ground and first floors with a tasting of three local wines paired with gougères in either the medieval kitchen or 15th-century cellar.
quote: discover and taste our wines... a famous wine Estate especially for its Chardonnay wines

claim: Château de Rully welcomes guests year-round; adult admission is €10 (free under 12), credit cards are not accepted, and in July-August visits are by appointment only, otherwise daily 10:45-18:00 in high season.
quote: Adults €10. Free for children under 12. Credit cards are not accepted... visits by appointment only in July and August.

claim: Château de Pommard (≈20 km north of Chagny) offers three booked tastings in 2026: Discover Burgundy €30/adult (4 cuvées, 1h), Clos Marey-Monge €41/adult, and Custom Tasting €94/adult (6 wines, private); reservation recommended.
quote: Discover Burgundy - €30/adult... Clos Marey Monge Tasting - €41/adult... Custom Tasting - €94/adult... 15 rue Marey Monge, 21630 Pommard

claim: Château du Clos de Vougeot, headquarters of the Confrérie des Chevaliers du Tastevin, is open daily in 2026: low season (Nov-Mar) 10:00-17:00, high season (Apr-Oct) 09:30-18:00; guided tour €15, self-guided free during opening hours, sensory experience €45.
quote: Low season (Nov 1 - Mar 31): 10h-17h. High season (Apr 1 - Oct 31): 9h30-18h. Guided tour: €15... Sensory experience: €45

claim: The Château du Clos de Vougeot sits in the village of Vougeot in the Côte de Nuits, about 25 km from Dijon — roughly 55-60 km north-east of Chagny by road, well BEYOND the 30 km radius.
quote: Clos de Vougeot is an Appellation d'origine contrôlée (AOC) for red wine in Burgundy... located in the village of Vougeot... Côte de Nuits

claim: Abbaye de Cîteaux is open 22 Apr–5 Jul and 29 Sep–1 Nov 2026, Wed-Sun 10:00-13:00 / 14:00-18:00; guided tours last 1h15 and reservations are essential, with a ten-minute walk from the parking to reception — but the abbey lies ~30 km from Beaune (so ~45-50 km from Chagny), beyond the 30 km radius.
quote: Tours are 1¼ hours and reservations are essential. There is about a ten-minute walk from the parking lot to the visitor reception.

claim: Château de Sully (in Sully, Saône-et-Loire — birthplace of Maréchal de MacMahon, not Vauban) is open daily 4 Apr–1 Nov 2026, 09:30-17:00; admission with guided tour of château plus park is €10.20 adults, €4.50 children, €29 family rate.
quote: open every day, including public holidays, from 04/04/2026 to 01/11/2026, from 9:30am to 5pm... Adults €10.20, Children €4.50, Large families €29

claim: Chagny's Tour Bajole is a 12th-century building once linked to the priory of Saint-Georges; it currently houses Maison Lameloise itself and is visible only from outside.
quote: As early as the 12th century, this building was dependent on the powerful priory of Saint George... Currently, it houses a gastronomic restaurant, and it is only visible from the outside.

claim: A guided 'Discovering Chagny' walking tour runs June-September on Tuesdays at 15:00, covering the 12th-13th-century Saint-Martin church and Romanesque bell tower, the 1715 hospital apothecary, and the 15th/18th-century towers.
quote: A guided tour 'Discovering Chagny' is available from June to September, Tuesdays at 3 p.m... Saint Martin church and its Romanesque bell tower... apothecary from 1715

claim: Beaune's Collégiale Notre-Dame is open daily 08:00-18:00 with free entry; its 15th-century Tournai tapestries of the Life of the Virgin are viewable April-October on Wed/Thu/Fri/Sun 14:30-17:30 and Sat 10:00-12:00 for a €3 guided fee.
quote: the tapestries are accessible by a €3 guided tour between April and mid-November... Wednesday-Thursday-Friday and Sunday: 2.30pm-5.30pm / Saturday 10am-12pm

claim: Voie des Vignes from Beaune to Santenay is 23 km, easy difficulty (149 m ascent), passing Pommard, Meursault and Chassagne-Montrachet, connecting at Santenay to the Canal du Centre greenway toward Chalon.

claim: EuroVelo 6 between Chalon-sur-Saône and Santenay runs 24 km along the Canal du Centre towpath, with Chagny's canal port sitting roughly halfway between Rully and Santenay.

claim: Les Cabottes in Change (between Santenay and Beaune, directly on the Voie des Vignes) rents e-bikes at €25 half-day / €45 full day, with child seats, trailers (€15/€25) and helmets included.
quote: Half-day: €25 (morning 9am-1pm or afternoon 2pm-6pm) and €45 for a full day

claim: Santenay Tourist Office rents standard and electric bikes, with e-bikes at €25 half-day / €35 full day.
quote: Electrically-assisted bikes cost €25 for a half day and €35 for a full day

claim: Bourgogne Randonnées in Beaune is the most-reviewed Burgundy bike-rental shop, offering classic, road and electric bikes for exploring the Côte de Beaune from a central Beaune location.
quote: Bike rental in Beaune in Côte d'Or (21)

claim: From Saint-Léger-sur-Dheune (about 15 km from Chagny) CrisBoat offers licence-free self-drive canal cruisers, including a 3-night round-trip to Chagny (26 km of canal).
quote: 3-night round trips to Chagny (26km) or Montchanin (38km)

claim: Locaboat operates a hire base in Saint-Léger-sur-Dheune on the Canal du Centre offering no-licence pénichettes after a 1-hour training session.
quote: Location bateau Canal du Centre & Saône

claim: Air Escargot launches from 25 Chemin du 6 Septembre 1944, Remigny (about 8 km from Chagny), with ~1.5-hour flights over Nuits-Saint-Georges, Beaune and Chalon-sur-Saône vineyards.
quote: flights last about an hour and a half

claim: Air Escargot prices are tiered: €240/person for 1–4 passengers, €220 for 5–8, €200 for 9+, with half price for under-12s, including post-flight aperitif and minibus transfer back.
quote: 240 euros per person (1-4 persons), 220 euros per person (5-8 persons), and 200 euros per person (9+ persons)

claim: France Montgolfières flies from Marigny-lès-Reullée near Beaune from 1 April to 31 October, at sunrise or two hours before sunset, with discovery flights priced €199–249 per person.
quote: Compris entre 199€ et 249€ (Discovery flight - 1 person)

quote: 1,247 parcels of vines, also known as "climats", carefully delimited over the centuries

claim: Beaune Tourism markets the Chemin des Grands Crus as the headline vineyard walk through Pommard, Meursault, Chassagne-Montrachet and Santenay, all within 30 km of Chagny.
quote: The Chemin des Grands Crus

claim: The GR de Pays des Grands Crus is the recognised long-distance footpath linking Dijon to Santenay through the Côte de Nuits and Côte de Beaune, usable in shorter loops from Meursault or Santenay.
quote: The Great Wines Trail - Grands Crus (Dijon to Santenay, Burgundy)

claim: Valvital's Spa Thermal de Santenay reopens for the 2026 season from 11 February to 27 December, with thermal cures running 16 March to 21 November and an Aqua-détente space (hot pool, hammam, sauna, caldarium).
quote: The Spa Thermal is open from February 11 to December 27, 2026

claim: Casino JOA de Santenay (5 km from Chagny) operates 150 slot machines, English roulette, blackjack and Ultimate Poker tables, open 9 am–2 am weekdays and to 4 am Fri/Sat, with its Comptoir JOA bistro restaurant.
quote: 150 slot machines

claim: Musée Nicéphore Niépce in Chalon-sur-Saône offers free entry ('entrée libre'), open Sep-Jun 9:30-11:45 and 14:00-17:45, Jul-Aug 10:00-13:00 and 14:00-18:00, closed Tuesdays and holidays.
quote: de septembre à juin 9h30 ... 11h45 / 14h ... 17h45 ... en juillet et août 10h ... 13h / 14h ... 18h ... entrée libre

claim: The Niépce museum houses Europe's most prestigious photographic collection — 3 million images and over 10,000 cameras and objects, including the 'Chambre de la Découverte', the first photographic camera in the world.
quote: le fonds photographique le plus prestigieux d'Europe. Ses collections rassemblent 3 millions d'images et plus de 10 000 appareils et objets ... la « Chambre de la Découverte », premier appareil photographique au monde

claim: Niépce captured 'View from the Window at Le Gras' — the world's first surviving photograph — at his estate in Saint-Loup-de-Varennes (5 km south of Chalon) circa 1826-1827.
quote: the so-called 'View from the Window at Le Gras' marked the beginning of photography as we know it. The image depicts the view from his estate in Saint-Loup-de-Varennes

claim: France is staging a year-long celebration in 2026 to mark 200 years of photography, with Chalon-sur-Saône central to events.
quote: France set to stage a year-long celebration to mark 200 years of photography in 2026

claim: Chalon-sur-Saône hosts food markets Friday and Sunday mornings plus an organic market Wednesday, selling Bresse poultry, Charolais beef, snails, wines, charcuterie, cheeses and produce.
quote: The Friday and Sunday morning markets, as well as the Wednesday morning organic market ... Bresse poultry to Charolais beef, snails, wines, charcuterie, cheeses, fruit and vegetables

claim: Chalon's Sunday market sprawls from Place Saint-Vincent to Place de Beaune with crowds so thick it can be hard to move; the half-timbered houses around Place Saint-Vincent frame the scene.
quote: On Sundays, crowds flock to the market from Place Saint-Vincent to Place de Beaune for food and other goods, often making it difficult to get around

claim: Cathédrale Saint-Vincent was built between 1090 and 1520, sits on Place Saint-Vincent surrounded by 15th-century half-timbered houses, with a neo-gothic west façade added in the 19th century.

quote: 115 hectares ... plus de 600 variétés de roses ... un parcours pédestre d'environ 3 km retrace l'histoire de la rose

claim: The Côte Chalonnaise has five village AOCs: Bouzeron (only AOC for Aligoté), Rully (whites and crémant centre, 23 premier crus), Mercurey (largest, 30 premier crus, mostly red), Givry (17 premier crus, mostly red), Montagny (whites only, 49 premier crus).
quote: Bouzeron, the only communal AOC for Aligoté still wine; Rully, which has 23 premier cru vineyards ... Mercurey, which with 30 premier cru vineyards is the largest volume producer ... Givry, whose 17 premier cru vineyards ... Montagny which produces only white wines and has 49 premier cru vineyards

claim: Caveau Givry Vins offers 30+ Côte Chalonnaise wines via a prepaid Enomatic card, open Wed-Sun 10:00-13:00 and 15:00-18:30 (Apr-Oct), with bottle prices €11-€38.50.
quote: tasting room equipped with an Enomatic system ... selection of over 30 wines ... open from April to end of October, Wednesday to Sunday from 10am to 1pm and 3pm to 6:30pm ... Prices range from €11 to €38.50

claim: Château de Chamirey in Mercurey, an 18th-century winery with 37 hectares (15 ha premiers crus), offers cellar tours and tastings from €0 to €55; the average Mercurey cellar tour with tasting is €40.
quote: The price of Château de Chamirey experiences varies between €0.00 and €55.00 ... in Mercurey, the average price of a cellar tour with wine tasting is €40.00

claim: Maison André Delorme in Rully runs 5 tasting formulas and shows the artisanal Crémant de Bourgogne process in its vaulted rock-carved cellars.
quote: 5 tasting formulas and discover the secrets of the artisanal process of making Crémants de Bourgogne ... vaulted cellars carved into the rock

claim: Vitteaut-Alberti in Rully has made Crémant traditionally since 1951 and offers a 1h45 'Immersion' tour with 6 tastings for €25 per person, booking essential, in French or English.

claim: Domaine A. et P. de Villaine in Bouzeron — founded 1973 by Aubert de Villaine (DRC co-director) — farms 30 ha organically since 1986 and biodynamically since 2000; nephew Pierre de Benoist now runs it.

claim: Bouzeron earned its village AOC for Aligoté in 1998 — the only village in Burgundy with this status — thanks to Aubert de Villaine's lobbying.
quote: Bouzeron received the Village AOC for Aligoté in 1998 as the only village in Burgundy to do so, thanks to Aubert de Villaine's commitment

claim: Cave des Vignerons de Buxy (founded 1931) is a 200-grower cooperative pouring all Côte Chalonnaise AOCs (Montagny, Givry, Rully, Mercurey) plus Crémant de Bourgogne, with free tastings.
quote: Created in 1931 ... 200 winemaker-cooperatives ... offers all the local appellations: Montagny, Givry, Rully, Mercurey, and Crémant de Bourgogne ... free tastings

claim: The cooperative's new visitor centre 'Maison Millebuis' adds a wine-tourism, sales and tasting hall plus a barrel cellar, with guided summer tours.
quote: Its new seminar space, wine tourism, sales and tasting area 'la Maison Millebuis' as well as its magnificent barrel cellar are essential to visit

claim: Château de Couches, an 11th-century Burgundy fortress linked by local tradition to Marguerite de Bourgogne, runs audio-guided or self-guided tours plus a wine-tasting cellar of estate wines and a gourmet restaurant.
quote: fortress with a thousand-year history ... a gourmet restaurant, a wine-tasting cellar to discover the domain's wines ... audio-guided or free visits

claim: Givry's flagship wine event is the annual Marché aux Vins held over a weekend in early April (the 30th edition ran April 5-7).
quote: 30ème édition du Marché aux Vins : 5, 6 & 7 avril

claim: Maison Lameloise is open Monday and Thursday through Sunday with lunch 12:00–13:00 and dinner 19:30–21:00; closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
quote: Monday, Thursday-Sunday: 12:00-13:00 (lunch) and 19:30-21:00 (dinner). Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

claim: Lameloise's Saturday seatings are noon–1pm for lunch and 7:30pm–9pm for dinner, confirming an 8pm reservation falls inside the standard dinner window.
quote: Sunday-Monday, Thursday-Saturday: 12PM-1PM and 7:30PM-9PM. Tuesday-Wednesday: Closed.

claim: A Lameloise tasting-menu service typically runs around five hours, with one diner reporting their evening lasted from 8pm to 1am.
quote: from 8pm to 1am

claim: The Hospices de Beaune (Hôtel-Dieu) opens daily including Sunday, running continuously 9:00–19:30 from April through mid-November, with last admission one hour before close.
quote: From April 1st to November 15th 2026, the Hôtel-Dieu is open continuously from 9AM to 7:30PM... last ticket office access is 1 hour before the site closes.

claim: Sunday is quiet across rural Burgundy: most shops are closed but several Beaune wine cellars (Patriarche, Bouchard Aîné, Marché aux Vins, Jaffelin) and outdoor sites stay open.
quote: Multiple cellars in Beaune operate Sundays, including Patriarche, Bouchard Aîné et Fils, Marché aux Vins, and Jaffelin... Most stores are closed.

claim: Chagny itself hosts a year-round Sunday morning market, providing a walkable Sunday option from a Chagny base when most of Burgundy is shut.
quote: Le marché de Chagny c'est tous les dimanches matins, même en hiver

claim: Chagny to Beaune is about 16 km / 32 minutes by car, putting Beaune comfortably in half-day range from Maison Lameloise.
quote: road distance from Chagny to Beaune is 9.75 miles or 15.69 kilometres, and a typical journey time for this route is 32 minutes

claim: Beaune to Château de La Rochepot is roughly 17 km / 17 minutes, so La Rochepot remains a comfortable half-day loop from Chagny via the Hautes-Côtes.

claim: Standard prep advice for a long Michelin tasting menu is to eat very lightly during the day and arrive hungry but rested, since courses are reduced in size but numerous.
quote: If you abstain from consuming calories during the day, you should be fine by the time you're headed for dinner. One approach is to only have a coffee or a tiny snack before the Michelin meal.

claim: The Mont de Sène (Montagne des Trois Croix) loop from Santenay starts at place du Jet d'Eau (223 m) in the village centre, climbs to a 521 m summit with three crosses and orientation tables, covers 10.7 km with 358 m cumulative ascent, and passes cliffs above the vines and the Bois de la Fée.
quote: Mont de Sène ou Montagne des Trois Croix (521m) par Santenay … place du Jet d'Eau, au centre du village (223m) … 10,7km … Dénivelé cumulé : 358m … tables d'orientation sur chacune de ses extrémités nord et sud … des falaises surplombant les vignes et le bois de la Fée
